clue.text: A foreign visitor's permit to see fathers' game

parts.note: fathers are pas, informal for dads
a sport is a game

explanation.surface: Dads take an overseas guest along to watch a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A travel document lets someone cross borders and enter another country.

clue.text: A drink taken at the railway station

explanation.surface: Someone has a drink while waiting for a train.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark beer is one sense; the other is the station employee who carries luggage.

clue.text: A nurse will make the connection

explanation.surface: A nurse will help someone get in touch.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a SISTER is a senior nurse in charge of a ward.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior ward nurse in Britain is called this; it also names a family relation, a connection by blood.

clue.text: Offering no resistance to infiltration

parts.note: reads like a weak military defence, but describes a material that lets water seep through

explanation.surface: A defence lets enemy agents slip in unopposed.
explanation.definitionFit: A permeable material lets liquid seep in freely.

clue.text: A beast might well get rich sooner

indicators.note: suggests the following words could be turned into something else, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An animal may become wealthy before long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might well get' signals rearranging RICH SOONER.
explanation.definitionFit: A large horned African or Asian mammal is a kind of animal.

clue.text: Temporary accommodation housing an occupant

indicators.note: the shelter holds the other word inside it

parts.note: a tent is a temporary shelter

explanation.surface: A camp shelter provides a place for someone to live.
explanation.definitionFit: A person renting and living in a property occupies it.

clue.text: Explains being out of cash?

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of, as in ex-works
pounds are British money

explanation.surface: Someone justifies themselves for being broke.
explanation.definitionFit: To set out a theory in detail is to explain it.

clue.text: Put in an appearance and was all ears

explanation.surface: Someone showed up and listened intently.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning up at an event is one sense; paying close heed to someone is the other.

clue.text: Stand, strange to relate

indicators.note: something strange is out of its normal order, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An odd tale is hard to bear.
explanation.definitionFit: To put up with something is to bear it, as in 'I can't bear him'.

clue.text: Hold back — come down after all the others

indicators.note: the falling word is placed after the other piece

parts.note: the rest means everyone remaining
rain comes down from the sky

explanation.surface: An instruction to wait and descend last of all.
explanation.definitionFit: To curb or check something is to keep it under control.

clue.text: Making pals, it appears, in a lazar-house

indicators.note: the letters given are used to make a new word, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Patients befriend each other in a leper colony.
explanation.walkthrough: A lazar is a leper; a spital is an old word for a hospital, especially for lepers.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for a hospital, particularly one for lepers.

clue.text: Will's been put in his charge

definitions.text: Will's been put in his charge

parts.words: Will's been put in his charge
parts.note: Will looks like a man's name, but it is a legal testament, entrusted to the person who carries it out

explanation.surface: A boy named Will has been placed in someone's care.
explanation.definitionFit: The person named in a testament to administer the estate.

clue.text: A painter has a go with little hesitation

parts.note: a turn is a go in a game
er is the short sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: An artist tries something, pausing a little.
explanation.walkthrough: J. M. W. Turner was a great English landscape painter.
explanation.definitionFit: An English Romantic artist famous for seascapes and light.

clue.text: A far-sighted person who knows when a fall is coming!

definitions.text: A far-sighted person who knows when a fall is coming!

parts.words: A far-sighted person who knows when a fall is coming!
parts.note: fall suggests a stumble or crash, but it means rain or snow, predicted by a weather expert

explanation.surface: A visionary anticipates a disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteorologist predicts weather such as rainfall.

clue.text: Scent bodes ill, and that's not so good!

indicators.note: bodes ill suggests bad luck, but ill signals the letters are badly arranged and must be reordered

explanation.surface: A bad smell is an omen of trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inferior to the best is lesser in quality.

clue.text: Raised outside before getting ridiculed

indicators.note: the first word sits around the second

parts.note: bred means brought up or raised
ante is Latin for before

explanation.surface: Someone brought up in front of others is mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: Teased playfully with jokes; mocked good-humouredly.

clue.text: The foreigner's street guide

parts.note: a ranger guides visitors around a park

explanation.surface: An outsider's map of a road.
explanation.definitionFit: An outsider or someone from elsewhere is unknown here.

clue.text: Maintain to prisoner that I am in tune — but off-beat

parts.note: con is short for convict

indicators.note: out of rhythm, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone insists to an inmate that their singing is in key though out of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I am in tune' puts I with TUNE; 'off-beat' rearranges them into TINUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep going or carry on with something.

clue.text: A scientist who finds work heavenly

definitions.text: A scientist who finds work heavenly

parts.words: A scientist who finds work heavenly
parts.note: heavenly seems to mean blissful, but means literally in the heavens, the sky

explanation.surface: A researcher loves their job.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who studies stars and planets.

clue.text: Burned deep red

parts.note: the deep is the ocean

explanation.surface: Something was scorched a dark crimson.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorched the surface of something with heat.

clue.text: The rope involved in a trial

indicators.note: tangled up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cord is evidence in a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is a looped cord used for catching cattle.

clue.text: In summer Germans arrange such a get-together

indicators.note: the letters lie within the next words

explanation.surface: In summer, Germans organise a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A combining of two firms into one is a union of businesses.

clue.text: Retrograde art and its peculiarities

indicators.note: moving backwards, so the word is read in reverse

explanation.surface: Backward-looking art has its odd features.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinctive characteristics or qualities of a person.

clue.text: Run-down old American?

parts.note: suggests an exhausted elderly citizen, but means someone white-faced, an old Native American term for a white settler

explanation.surface: A tired elderly person from the US.
explanation.definitionFit: A term once used in Westerns for a white person.

clue.text: Soldiers with spirit accompanying a queen

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
gin is an alcoholic spirit

explanation.surface: Troops with a drink escort a royal.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'a queen' takes the A as part of it, and the A of the wordplay comes from 'a' too; REGINA is Latin for queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for a female monarch, as on coins and legal documents.

clue.text: Looking about right, so taking the lead

indicators.note: the looking word surrounds the other

parts.note: staring means looking hard

explanation.surface: Gazing around properly, someone leads.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing the principal role in a film or play.

clue.text: "Mended" as an interjection?

explanation.surface: Someone asks if 'mended' could be used as an exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Repaired a sock with needle and thread; also a mild oath meaning damned.

clue.text: Quietly trade or exchange a hunter

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for softly

indicators.note: swap around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Discreet bartering for a hunter.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal that kills and eats others for food.
